From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2028-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity translation for Silverthorn — tokens/sec -> GPU plan

Kevin / team — thanks again for the call this morning. Sharing a concise summary and the ask so our capacity team can map your expected token load to a recommended Dedicated slab + headroom plan. I attached the PDF you shared during the demo.

Quick summary of what you told us:
- Target model: Llama-3-70B (int8 quantized runtime).
- Performance SLO: p95 generation latency <= 150ms for single-request flows.
- Expected traffic: interactive product — peak ~40 requests/sec, median concurrency ~30, median tokens/request (prompt+completion) ~700 tokens.
- Daily volume: rough 10M tokens/day initially, ramp to ~60M/day over 3 months.
- Prefers Dedicated for isolation and predictable billing; interested in burst capacity option.

Ask from us (can you confirm the items below?):
1) Are the 40 req/sec peaks single-region (US-West) only?
2) Any heavy multi-turn usage that would reuse KV cache across requests (session affinity)?
3) Is model pinning required (non-negotiable version) or are you open to compatible lower-footprint variants for overflow?

What I need from our infra folks: a tokens/sec translation (tokens/sec = requests/sec * tokens/request) -> GPUs required for sustained + 2x headroom -> suggested slab size and burst cushion. Also a recommended fallback (smaller quantized variant or cross-region routing) if sustained peaks exceed capacity.

Attaching: Silverthorn_MVP_request.pdf (you shared the product doc). I’ll loop infra and karthik for the calc.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Capacity translation for Silverthorn — tokens/sec -> GPU plan

Vanessa — thanks, this is clear. Doing a first-pass translation with the assumptions below; marking unknowns where I need confirmation from Silverthorn.

Assumptions:
- Peak: 40 req/sec * 700 tokens/request = 28,000 tokens/sec peak.
- Model: Llama-3-70B int8 — steady-state throughput we observe on an H100-80GB (optimized kernels) is ~5.5k tokens/sec per GPU for worst-case latency under 150ms p95 for this model/config (single-request, no batching). With aggressive async batching and KV reuse that can rise to ~9k tokens/sec/GPU.

Rough mappings (peak sustained):
- No KV reuse, conservative: 28,000 / 5.5k ≈ 5.1 GPUs -> recommend 6 GPUs (sustained).
- If we count 2x headroom for burst/resilience and scheduling noise: 6 * 2 = 12 GPUs.
- If KV reuse / batching applies (typical chat sessions with session affinity): 28,000 / 9k ≈ 3.1 -> recommend 4 GPUs sustained, 8 GPUs with 2x headroom.

Practical slab proposals: (mix of cost vs latency trade-offs)
- Conservative Dedicated slab: 12x H100-80GB (covers peak + 2x headroom, simple routing).
- Cost-optimized slab: 8x H100-80GB + burst pool (shared preemptible capacity) — needs canary + fallback to quantized 4-bit variant under queue.
- Hybrid: 6x H100 + 4x A100-80GB in burst pool (cheaper burst but requires cross-GPU routing).

Questions for Silverthorn (to confirm final numbers):
- Can you share the expected session affinity percentage? (i.e., what fraction of requests reuse an open session/kv cache?)
- Are you comfortable with an overflow policy that routes overflow to a quantized 4-bit variant with slightly higher p95?

I’ll prepare a short spreadsheet with token->GPU math and a cost delta between the slab options once we get the affinity number.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Note: these are initial ballpark figures; final recommended slab will include autoscaling/burst margins and latency tail tests in our staging cluster.

I attached a short MAP doc and the original brief. If these dates work I’ll also create the HubSpot timeline.

Vanessa / Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. Confirming the details you asked about:

- Region: US-West primary for initial rollout (we may add EU later).
- Session affinity: ~65% of interactive traffic will reuse a session (so KV cache reuse is common).
- Model pinning: we prefer a pinned Llama-3-70B for initial GA, but we can accept an overflow flow to a quantized 4-bit variant during sustained peaks if performance delta is documented.

We’re good with the MAP timeline. Please send the spreadsheet and the conservative vs cost-optimized slab options. Also please include a short note on expected cold-starts (token penalty) when adding new VMs for burst.

Cheers,
